A tempting metric is "publications per dollar." It is also easy to get wrong:
shared-facility **center cores** accumulate acknowledgments from everyone using
them and dominate a naïve ranking, and the metric has a built-in **age bias**
(older grants have had longer to publish). This notebook uses the
`pubs_per_dollar` tool, which groups support-years into core grants, splits by
**mechanism family**, and **discloses** its denominator and any cap.

```{python}
from nih_science_agent.tools.productivity import pubs_per_dollar, mechanism_family
```

## A fair cohort: NIAID DP2 (New Innovator) awards

DP2 awards share a fixed budget, so pubs-per-\$ is an apples-to-apples
comparison within the cohort.

```{python}
report = pubs_per_dollar(
    institutes=["NIAID"], mechanisms=["DP2"], fiscal_years=list(range(2015, 2025)),
    funding_floor=500_000,
)
print(f"{report.records_matched} records → {report.grants_matched} grants; "
      f"analyzed {report.grants_analyzed}")
for note in report.notes:
    print("  ⚠", note)

print(f"\n{'pubs/$1M':>9}  {'pubs':>4}  {'cum $':>12}  core")
for grant in report.results[:8]:
    ppm = f"{grant.pubs_per_million:.1f}" if grant.pubs_per_million else "n/a"
    print(f"{ppm:>9}  {grant.publication_count:>4}  ${grant.total_funding:>11,.0f}  "
          f"{grant.core_project_num}")
```

## Why the mechanism split matters

Run it across mechanisms on a topic and the center cores leap to the top of the
raw ranking — an attribution artifact, not real productivity:

```{python}
mixed = pubs_per_dollar(query="PFAS", institutes=["NIEHS"],
                        fiscal_years=list(range(2015, 2025)), funding_floor=500_000)

def top(fam, n=4):
    rows = [r for r in mixed.results if r.mechanism_family == fam]
    return [(round(r.pubs_per_million, 1), r.core_project_num, r.activity_code) for r in rows[:n]]

print("center_core (inflated by shared-facility acknowledgments):")
for r in top("center_core"): print("  ", r)
print("research (the apples-to-apples comparison):")
for r in top("research"): print("  ", r)
```

The classifier is a transparent heuristic:

```{python}
{code: mechanism_family(code) for code in ["R01", "DP2", "P30", "U19", "T32", "K23"]}
```

> **Caveat.** Even within a mechanism, pubs-per-\$ favors older grants (more
> time to publish) and undercounts publications that don't cite the grant
> (RePORTER attribution is incomplete). Use it to compare *within* a cohort, not
> to crown a winner.
